cohort: The study included children born in Denmark between 1992 and 2002, with neonatal vitamin D measurements, where cases were children diagnosed with asthma and the sub-cohort was randomly selected from all children born in the same period.
finding: Higher neonatal vitamin D concentrations (fifth quintile) were associated with a significantly reduced risk (hazard ratio 0.55) of developing asthma between ages 3 and 9 years compared to children in the first quintile.
